gaps: Claude-mode writes have no stated canonical brief or `forge delegate` preparation step. A writer entry alone drops the existing brief gate without naming replacement authority (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:271; docs/specs/delegation-boundary.md:36; docs/specs/delegation-boundary.md:66).

Claude-only mode promises no Codex dependency, but the plan does not say how either doctor path stops requiring the Codex CLI and plugin or attempting their repair (docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:29; .factory/grill-brief-plan.md:271; factory/scripts/forge_cli/doctor.py:1139; factory/scripts/forge_cli/doctor.py:1840).

An exported `FORGE_EXECUTOR` can override `.envrc` per machine, yet the plan has no rule for changing executor mode during an active task or excluding a Claude writer while a Codex turn holds that task. Existing companion exclusion covers launch locks, not the proposed Claude writer entry (docs/decisions/0085-executor-modes.md:20; .factory/grill-brief-plan.md:271; factory/scripts/forge_cli/delegate.py:551).

The SDK supervisor may host multiple task threads, but the plan does not explain how a hook caller is bound to its exact turn and task. Today's admission authenticates one launch through environment selectors, process ancestry, a matching lock, and a brief; a supervisor-wide token would not establish per-turn scope (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:292; factory/scripts/forge_cli/worker_admission.py:287; factory/scripts/forge_cli/worker_admission.py:329).

The per-turn ledger's durable location and merge behavior are unstated. Task worktrees can disappear after merge, while archival, doctor retries, and pruning must still find their thread IDs (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:294; .factory/grill-brief-plan.md:309; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:86).

A resolution is counted as delivered when its carrying turn starts, without proof that `turn/steer` succeeded or the resumed worker received it. A turn can start and finish before the message arrives, allowing close to treat an unanswered signal as delivered (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:304; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:71).

`--abandon-turn` can mark an unreadable turn failed without a stated revocation and verified worker-process cleanup. The existing companion route records terminal failure only after it has reaped the observed process tree; otherwise a later successful turn could let close pass while the abandoned writer remains live (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:307; factory/scripts/forge_cli/delegate.py:2278; factory/scripts/forge_cli/delegate.py:2329).

The plan says client upgrades wait for open D-0040, but gives UPGRADE-CLEANUP no dependency or release check that establishes the hold was lifted. Its upgrade deliverable can therefore be declared complete while the named client-rollout prerequisite remains open (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:310; .factory/grill-brief-plan.md:332; plans/deferrals.md:48).

The documentation list omits README.md, docs/degraded-mode.md, and the Claude adapter, all of which still tell users that the plugin is Claude's only route or that Claude cannot write product code. Leaving them as shipped would give users instructions that contradict the new modes (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:313; README.md:33; docs/degraded-mode.md:3; .claude/CLAUDE.md:8).

SDK-ADMISSION turns the new route on before LIVE-EVENTS supplies streaming, reattachment, and signal steering. During the independently shipped interval, users can start SDK workers but cannot use the promised live supervision or reliably answer their signals; the plan needs an activation rule for that interval (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:316; .factory/grill-brief-plan.md:329; .factory/grill-brief-plan.md:331; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:67).

The benchmark has no named durable evidence artifact or recorder for its trial identities, token counts, wall times, and medians. Story proof currently consists only of a short outcome paragraph, so the proposed numbers cannot be checked as the required recorded story evidence (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:340; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:104; AGENTS.md:85; factory/schemas/outcome.json:11).

The resumed benchmark trials depend on forks of a saved worker thread, but the plan does not name a supported fork operation or say how each trial starts from the same pre-fix thread state. Without that, its three warm replays are not reproducible evidence for the required resumed fix-round comparison (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:340; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:104).

The platform proof calls for pytest cells on Ubuntu and Windows and one real task per mode on macOS, but does not require the real runner-OS launcher, SDK app-server, hook and recovery exercise, pinned CLI version/help record, or local Mac Desktop observation specified by Decision 0065. Passing cells alone would not establish the claimed cross-platform route parity (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:343; docs/decisions/0065-ci-platform-evidence.md:18; docs/decisions/0065-ci-platform-evidence.md:26).
contradictions: The claim that Codex workers retain full access 'as today' also covers the plugin fallback, whose current official companion remains workspace-write/read-only under Decision 0081. The plan needs to distinguish the full-access SDK route from that fallback (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:233; docs/decisions/0081-full-access-for-forge-managed-codex-chats.md:18; docs/decisions/0081-full-access-for-forge-managed-codex-chats.md:43).

Deferring Claude writes for a single hybrid task contradicts accepted Decision 0085 and the confirmed capability spec, which explicitly admit Claude execution in hybrid mode. D-0044 records a deferral but does not identify replacement authority for those binding contracts (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:233; .factory/grill-brief-plan.md:277; docs/decisions/0085-executor-modes.md:24; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:32; plans/deferrals.md:52).

Refusing every non-Codex executor setting when Codex coordinates contradicts Decision 0085's independent coordinator and executor settings, including Claude-only execution. The promised three-mode parity would omit those combinations (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:271; docs/decisions/0085-executor-modes.md:20; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:29).

The plan both makes task routes sticky, with a broken route refusing or requiring a recorded fresh restart, and says an unhealthy supervisor or version mismatch selects the plugin before dispatch. For a task already bound to SDK, these rules prescribe opposite outcomes (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:288; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:40; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:81).
resolutions: Claude writes still go through forge delegate / forge fix, which compose the canonical brief and record the Claude writer entry (Technical approach).

Claude-only mode promises no Codex dependency, but the plan does not say how either doctor path stops requiring the Codex CLI and plugin or attempting their repair (docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:29; .factory/grill-brief-plan.md:271; factory/scripts/forge_cli/doctor.py:1139; factory/scripts/forge_cli/doctor.py:1840).

An exported `FORGE_EXECUTOR` can override `.envrc` per machine, yet the plan has no rule for changing executor mode during an active task or excluding a Claude writer while a Codex turn holds that task. Existing companion exclusion covers launch locks, not the proposed Claude writer entry (docs/decisions/0085-executor-modes.md:20; .factory/grill-brief-plan.md:271; factory/scripts/forge_cli/delegate.py:551).

The SDK supervisor may host multiple task threads, but the plan does not explain how a hook caller is bound to its exact turn and task. Today's admission authenticates one launch through environment selectors, process ancestry, a matching lock, and a brief; a supervisor-wide token would not establish per-turn scope (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:292; factory/scripts/forge_cli/worker_admission.py:287; factory/scripts/forge_cli/worker_admission.py:329).

The per-turn ledger's durable location and merge behavior are unstated. Task worktrees can disappear after merge, while archival, doctor retries, and pruning must still find their thread IDs (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:294; .factory/grill-brief-plan.md:309; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:86).

A resolution is counted as delivered when its carrying turn starts, without proof that `turn/steer` succeeded or the resumed worker received it. A turn can start and finish before the message arrives, allowing close to treat an unanswered signal as delivered (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:304; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:71).

`--abandon-turn` can mark an unreadable turn failed without a stated revocation and verified worker-process cleanup. The existing companion route records terminal failure only after it has reaped the observed process tree; otherwise a later successful turn could let close pass while the abandoned writer remains live (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:307; factory/scripts/forge_cli/delegate.py:2278; factory/scripts/forge_cli/delegate.py:2329).

The plan says client upgrades wait for open D-0040, but gives UPGRADE-CLEANUP no dependency or release check that establishes the hold was lifted. Its upgrade deliverable can therefore be declared complete while the named client-rollout prerequisite remains open (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:310; .factory/grill-brief-plan.md:332; plans/deferrals.md:48).

The documentation list omits README.md, docs/degraded-mode.md, and the Claude adapter, all of which still tell users that the plugin is Claude's only route or that Claude cannot write product code. Leaving them as shipped would give users instructions that contradict the new modes (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:313; README.md:33; docs/degraded-mode.md:3; .claude/CLAUDE.md:8).

SDK-ADMISSION turns the new route on before LIVE-EVENTS supplies streaming, reattachment, and signal steering. During the independently shipped interval, users can start SDK workers but cannot use the promised live supervision or reliably answer their signals; the plan needs an activation rule for that interval (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:316; .factory/grill-brief-plan.md:329; .factory/grill-brief-plan.md:331; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:67).

The benchmark has no named durable evidence artifact or recorder for its trial identities, token counts, wall times, and medians. Story proof currently consists only of a short outcome paragraph, so the proposed numbers cannot be checked as the required recorded story evidence (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:340; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:104; AGENTS.md:85; factory/schemas/outcome.json:11).

The resumed benchmark trials depend on forks of a saved worker thread, but the plan does not name a supported fork operation or say how each trial starts from the same pre-fix thread state. Without that, its three warm replays are not reproducible evidence for the required resumed fix-round comparison (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:340; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:104).

The platform proof calls for pytest cells on Ubuntu and Windows and one real task per mode on macOS, but does not require the real runner-OS launcher, SDK app-server, hook and recovery exercise, pinned CLI version/help record, or local Mac Desktop observation specified by Decision 0065. Passing cells alone would not establish the claimed cross-platform route parity (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:343; docs/decisions/0065-ci-platform-evidence.md:18; docs/decisions/0065-ci-platform-evidence.md:26).

The claim that Codex workers retain full access 'as today' also covers the plugin fallback, whose current official companion remains workspace-write/read-only under Decision 0081. The plan needs to distinguish the full-access SDK route from that fallback (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:233; docs/decisions/0081-full-access-for-forge-managed-codex-chats.md:18; docs/decisions/0081-full-access-for-forge-managed-codex-chats.md:43).

Deferring Claude writes for a single hybrid task contradicts accepted Decision 0085 and the confirmed capability spec, which explicitly admit Claude execution in hybrid mode. D-0044 records a deferral but does not identify replacement authority for those binding contracts (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:233; .factory/grill-brief-plan.md:277; docs/decisions/0085-executor-modes.md:24; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:32; plans/deferrals.md:52).

Refusing every non-Codex executor setting when Codex coordinates contradicts Decision 0085's independent coordinator and executor settings, including Claude-only execution. The promised three-mode parity would omit those combinations (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:271; docs/decisions/0085-executor-modes.md:20; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:29).

The plan both makes task routes sticky, with a broken route refusing or requiring a recorded fresh restart, and says an unhealthy supervisor or version mismatch selects the plugin before dispatch. For a task already bound to SDK, these rules prescribe opposite outcomes (.factory/grill-brief-plan.md:288; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:40; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:81).
